opex.note: Selling the platform and winning new merchants. Up 6% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and new commerce and AI features. Down 29% YoY, from $440M a year ago.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Down 53% YoY, from $214M a year ago.

opex.name: Transaction and loan losses
opex.note: Losses on merchant loans and cash advances, and transaction losses. Up 32% YoY as more sales flowed through Shopify Payments.

follow100Note: Subscription plans bring in $24.49 of every $100 and merchant solutions $75.51 — mostly a cut of merchants' sales. Direct costs take $50.47 and running the business takes another $36.06, leaving $13.48 of operating profit per $100. Investment gains and interest added $20.57, partly offset by a $2.24 loss on the Flexport stake and $1.17 of tax, so Shopify kept $30.64 of every $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: The earnings release prints a condensed statement (operating income $289M, other income $393M, net income $657M); the split of that $393M into a $368M net gain on equity and other investments and a $48M loss on the equity-method investment in Flexport comes from the non-GAAP reconciliation in the same release.
oneTimers: $368M net gain on equity and other investments — a paper gain as the value of Shopify's listed holdings rose during the quarter. Excluding equity investments, adjusted net income was $441M (non-GAAP) versus $657M GAAP net income.
$48M net loss on Shopify's equity-method investment in Flexport.

Stock-based compensation of $103M — a non-cash expense inside operating expenses. It is recurring, not one-off, but it is paid in shares rather than cash, so it does not reduce the $446M of free cash flow Shopify generated.
The $1,340M impairment on the sale of Shopify's logistics businesses was booked earlier in 2023, not in Q4 — it is why full-year net income was only $132M despite this quarter's $657M profit.
otherDetail: Other income of $393M in total: a $368M net gain on equity and other investments, partly offset by a $48M net loss on the equity-method investment in Flexport, with the remaining $73M from interest income, foreign exchange and other items. The $48M equity-method loss is the separate equityM line; the rest nets to otherIncomeM of $441M.
pngFooterNote: Profit is back — investment gains added $368M on top.

segments.name: Subscription solutions
segments.note: The monthly plans merchants pay to run their stores on Shopify. Up 31% YoY; monthly recurring revenue reached $149M, up 35%.

segments.name: Merchant solutions
segments.note: Mostly payment processing (Shopify Payments) — a cut of the sales flowing through merchants' stores — plus shipping and other merchant services. Up 21% YoY and 76% of all revenue; Shopify Payments processed 60% of GMV ($45.1B).

sources.label: Form 40-F — 2023 annual report, Exhibit 13 MD&A (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 24% to $2.14B as GMV grew 23% to $75.1B — 30% revenue growth after adjusting for the sale of the logistics businesses. Subscription revenue grew 31% to $525M on more merchants and higher plan prices, with monthly recurring revenue up 35% to $149M, while merchant solutions rose 21% to $1.62B as Shopify Payments processed 60% of GMV ($45.1B).
takeaways.title: Growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: Operating income was $289M (13% margin) versus a $188M loss a year ago. On an adjusted basis, operating income was $396M (18% margin), and gross margin widened to 49.5% from 46.0% as the dilutive logistics business exited. R&D fell 29% and G&A fell 53% after 2023's cost cuts, and free cash flow jumped to $446M, a 21% margin versus 5% a year ago.
takeaways.title: Operating profit returned

takeaways.text: Net income was $657M, but $368M of it was a net gain on equity investments — paper gains as listed holdings rose — plus interest income. Excluding equity investments, adjusted net income was $441M, and a $48M loss on the Flexport stake was a further drag. The operating business earned $289M; the investment gains added more than the operations did.
takeaways.title: Investments flattered the bottom line

verdict: Shopify swung to a $657M profit in Q4 as revenue grew 24% to $2.1B — and a $368M gain on its investments supplied more than half of the bottom line.
